Found 10 relevant papers on 'How are photon redshift and propagation direction determined by conserved spatial momenta in a diagonal Bianchi I universe, and what quadrupolar radiation anisotropy is generated by small traceless homogeneous shear?'.


1. Light propagation in a homogeneous and anisotropic universe
   ID: pxx0dy5l6y6o
   2022 · Fleury, Pierre, Pitrou, Cyril, Uzan, Jean-Philippe
   DOI: 10.48550/arxiv.1410.8473
   Abstract: This article proposes a comprehensive analysis of light propagation in an anisotropic and spatially homogeneous Bianchi I universe. After recalling that null geodesics are easily determined in such a spacetime, we derive the expressions of the redshift and direction drifts of light sources; by solving analytically the Sachs equation, we then obtain an explicit expression of the Jacobi matrix describing the propagation of narrow light beams. As a byproduct, we recover the old formula by Saunders for the angular diameter distance in a Bianchi I spacetime, but our derivation goes further since it also provides the optical shear and rotation. These results pave the way to the analysis of both supernovae data and weak lensing by the large-scale structure in Bianchi universes. 

2. Light propagation in a homogeneous and anisotropic universe
   ID: x4yo2kto68
   2015 · Pierre Fleury, Cyril Pitrou, Jean-Philippe Uzan · Physical Review D
   DOI: 10.1103/PHYSREVD.91.043511
   Abstract: This article proposes a comprehensive analysis of light propagation in an anisotropic and spatially homogeneous Bianchi I universe After recalling that null geodesics are easily determined in such a spacetime, we derive the expressions of the redshift and direction drifts of light sources; by solving analytically the Sachs equation, we then obtain an explicit expression of the Jacobi matrix describing the propagation of narrow light beams As a by-product, we recover the old formula by Saunders for the angular diameter distance in a Bianchi I spacetime, but our derivation goes further since it also provides the optical shear and rotation These results pave the way to the analysis of both supernovae data and weak lensing by the large-scale structure in Bianchi universes

3. Direction and redshift drifts for general observers and their applications in cosmology
   ID: qpxiebmfkdvu
   2022 · Pitrou, Cyril, Uzan, Jean-Philippe, Pereira, Thiago S.
   DOI: 10.48550/arxiv.1805.12121
   Abstract: High precision astrometry now enables to measure the time drift of astrophysical observables in real time, hence providing new ways to probe different cosmological models. This article presents a general derivation of the redshift and direction drifts for general observers. It is then applied to the standard cosmological framework of a Friedmann-Lemaitre space- time including all effects at first order in the cosmological perturbations, as well as in the class of spatially anisotropic universe models of the Bianchi I family. It shows that for a general observer, the direction drift splits into a parallax and an aberration drifts and order of magnitude estimates of these two components are provided. The multipolar decomposition of the redshift and aberration drifts is also derived and shows that the observer's peculiar velocity contributes only as a dipole whereas the anisotropic shear contributes as a quadrupole. 

4. Direction and redshift drifts for general observers and their applications in cosmology
   ID: 216ja18aox
   2018 · Oton H. Marcori, Cyril Pitrou, Jean-Philippe Uzan · Physical Review D
   DOI: 10.1103/PHYSREVD.98.023517
   Abstract: High precision astrometry now enables us to measure the time drift of astrophysical observables in real time, hence providing new ways to probe different cosmological models. This article presents a general derivation of the redshift and direction drifts for general observers. It is then applied to the standard cosmological framework of a Friedmann-Lema\^{\i}tre spacetime including all effects at first order in the cosmological perturbations, as well as in the class of spatially anisotropic universe models of the Bianchi I family. It shows that for a general observer, the direction drift splits into a parallax and an aberration drifts and order of magnitude estimates of these two components are provided. The multipolar decomposition of the redshift and aberration drifts is also derived and shows that the observer's peculiar velocity contributes only as a dipole whereas the anisotropic shear contributes as a quadrupole.

5. Shear-Free Gravitational Waves in an Anisotropic Universe
   ID: qk9h3eie5qcz
   2022
   DOI: 10.48550/arxiv.gr-qc/0210099
   Abstract: We study gravitational waves propagating through an anisotropic Bianchi I dust-filled universe (containing the Einstein-de-Sitter universe as a special case). The waves are modeled as small perturbations of this background cosmological model and we choose a family of null hypersurfaces in this space-time to act as the histories of the wavefronts of the radiation. We find that the perturbations we generate can describe pure gravitational radiation if and only if the null hypersurfaces are shear-free. We calculate the gauge-invariant small perturbations explicitly in this case. How these differ from the corresponding perturbations when the background space-time is isotropic is clearly exhibited. 

6. Shear-free gravitational waves in an anisotropic universe
   ID: nwcc92jer3
   2002 · Peter A. Hogan, E. M. O’Shea · Physical Review D
   DOI: 10.1103/PHYSREVD.66.124016
   Abstract: We study gravitational waves propagating through an anisotropic Bianchi type I dust-filled universe (containing the Einstein\char21{}de Sitter universe as a special case). The waves are modeled as small perturbations of this background cosmological model and we choose a family of null hypersurfaces in this space-time to act as the histories of the wave fronts of the radiation. We find that the perturbations we generate can describe pure gravitational radiation if and only if the null hypersurfaces are shear-free. We calculate the gauge-invariant small perturbations explicitly in this case. How these differ from the corresponding perturbations when the background space-time is isotropic is clearly exhibited.

7. The Origin of Cosmological Redshift in Spin Exchange Vacuum Compactification and Nonzero Rest Mass Photon Anisotropy
   ID: 4xfuswt17w
   1998 · Richard L Amoroso, Menas Kafatos, Paule Ecimovic
   DOI: 10.1007/978-94-017-0990-3_2
   Abstract: Einstein’s refinement of Newtonian gravitation repeated for General Relativity (GR) by quantum cosmology requires inflationary models of the universe to be critically reevaluated; the Hubble redshift is shown not to result from Doppler velocity, but anisotropic coupling to vacuum zero point fluctuations through harmonic structure described in terms of the Wheeler — Feynman absorber theory of radiation in the context of a Dirac vacuum and compactification dynamics. The quantum gravity of the comoving hyperstructure of a universe topologically both open and closed like a Klein bottle, also implies that frequency shift in photon propagation over cosmological distances is an inherent part of the spin exchange process, removing the ad hoc criticism of the well known Vigier theory of ‘tired light’.

8. Late-Time Tilted Anisotropic Relaxation: A Bianchi Type I Model Unifying the 2025 Cosmic Dipole Anomaly and DESI Evolving Dark Energy Hints
   ID: szj1uyv68nuc
   2026 · Britt B
   DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.18176835
   Abstract: Late-2025 observations have elevated the cosmic dipole anomaly to >5σ significance in multiple catalogs, challenging the isotropic FLRW foundation of ΛCDM. Concurrently, DESI Year-3+ data prefer a dynamical dark energy equation-of-state weakening at low redshift (~4.2σ). Emerging evidence suggests dipolar modulation in local H0 measurements. We propose a minimal tilted Bianchi Type I model with late-time anisotropic relaxation, where primordial shear (super-horizon relic) decays as σ ∝ a^{-3} but creates a transient “relaxation window” during cosmic acceleration. This geometric mechanism unifies the dipole excess, transient w_eff(z) deviation, and directional H0 variance without new fields. Predictions include dipole fade with redshift, axis alignments, and w_eff(z) contours testable with 2026 Euclid, Rubin, and DESI releases. 

9. Late-Time Tilted Anisotropic Relaxation: A Bianchi Type I Model Unifying the 2025 Cosmic Dipole Anomaly and DESI Evolving Dark Energy Hints
   ID: 0q3pyrz4srpc
   2026 · Britt B
   DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.18176834
   Abstract: Late-2025 observations have elevated the cosmic dipole anomaly to >5σ significance in multiple catalogs, challenging the isotropic FLRW foundation of ΛCDM. Concurrently, DESI Year-3+ data prefer a dynamical dark energy equation-of-state weakening at low redshift (~4.2σ). Emerging evidence suggests dipolar modulation in local H0 measurements. We propose a minimal tilted Bianchi Type I model with late-time anisotropic relaxation, where primordial shear (super-horizon relic) decays as σ ∝ a^{-3} but creates a transient “relaxation window” during cosmic acceleration. This geometric mechanism unifies the dipole excess, transient w_eff(z) deviation, and directional H0 variance without new fields. Predictions include dipole fade with redshift, axis alignments, and w_eff(z) contours testable with 2026 Euclid, Rubin, and DESI releases. 

10. Kinematics in spatially flat FLRW space-time.
   ID: 3csiw5h7rg
   2021 · Ion I. Cotaescu · arXiv: General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology
   Abstract: The kinematics on spatially flat FLRW space-times is presented for the first time in co-moving local charts with physical coordinates, i e the cosmic time and Painlev\' e-type Cartesian space coordinates It is shown that there exists a conserved momentum which determines the form of the covariant four-momentum on geodesics in terms of physical coordinates Moreover, with the help of the conserved momentum one identifies the peculiar momentum separating the peculiar and recessional motions without ambiguities It is shown that the energy and peculiar momentum satisfy the mass-shell condition of special relativity while the recessional momentum does not produce energy In this framework, the measurements of the kinetic quantities along geodesic performed by different observers are analysed pointing out an energy loss of the massive particles similar to that giving the photon redshift The examples of the kinematics on the de Sitter expanding universe and a new Milne-type space-time are extensively analysed
